question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(75,0.55),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X=37).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-1.2\,$ $\,0.1151\,$ $\,0.1131\,$ $\,0.1112\,$
$\,-1.1\,$ $\,0.1357\,$ $\,0.1335\,$ $\,0.1314\,$
$\,-1.0\,$ $\,0.1587\,$ $\,0.1562\,$ $\,0.1539\,$
$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-0.9\,$ $\,0.1685\,$ $\,0.1660\,$ $\,0.1635\,$
$\,-0.8\,$ $\,0.1949\,$ $\,0.1922\,$ $\,0.1894\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2236\,$ $\,0.2206\,$ $\,0.2177\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=75$ and $p=0.55.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =75\cdot 0.55 \\  & =41.25 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =75\cdot (1-0.55) \\  & =33.75 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(75)(0.55)=41.25
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(75)(0.55)(1-0.55)=18.56.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(41.25,18.56).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=37).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=37)≈P(36.5\le Y\le 37.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(36.5\le Y\le 37.5) & =P(\frac{36.5-41.25}{\sqrt{18.56}}\le Z\le \frac{37.5-41.25}{\sqrt{18.56}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.10\le Z\le -0.87) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.87)-P(Z<-1.10) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.87)-P(Z\le -1.10) \\  & =Φ(-0.87)-Φ(-1.10) \\  & =0.1922-0.1357 \\  & =0.0565\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=37)≈0.057
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0569.$
